description: Premium architectural rendering with strong structural definition, bold but controlled tonal depth, rich accurate color, crisp material detail, and clear commercial thumbnail impact.
editing_goals: Create a professionally finished architectural image with strong geometry, clear visual hierarchy, and immediate commercial impact
Build deliberate tonal separation with clean highlights, defined shadows, confident white points, and substantial but controlled black depth
Render stone, concrete, glass, metal, wood, brick, and painted surfaces with crisp but realistic texture
Enhance dimensional depth between foreground, structure, sky, and surrounding environment
Maintain accurate material color while allowing richer, more polished color than a neutral technical correction
Produce a result that is visibly stronger than the unedited RAW preview without creating an artificial HDR appearance
cautions: Avoid harsh local contrast, halos, edge glow, and crunchy texture
Do not use excessive Clarity or Dehaze on smooth walls, glass, reflective surfaces, or atmospheric backgrounds
Keep composition cropping conservative unless it clearly improves geometry, symmetry, balance, or edge cleanliness
Apply rotational leveling only when supported by reliable structural references
Distinguish camera roll from perspective convergence; CropAngle cannot correct converging verticals
Preserve highlight detail in windows, reflective metal, white facades, and bright skies
Avoid blocked shadows that hide structural detail
Avoid lifeless neutral rendering, weak material definition, or timid tonal separation

guidance: Use reliable structural horizontal and vertical references with high sensitivity to accidental camera roll
Prioritize rooflines, floor lines, window rows, facade edges, and clearly horizontal architectural elements
Distinguish rotational tilt from perspective convergence caused by camera position or wide-angle lenses
Do not use leaning trees, irregular masonry, decorative diagonals, or converging verticals as leveling references
Do not over-correct an intentional architectural viewpoint or deliberate dynamic composition
